title: Strengthen dist_eq_computable to a BFS fuel invariant
intent: Identify the abstract graph distance `G.dist u v` with the executable breadth-first-search distance `computable_dist G u v` by strengthening the goal to an invariant statement about the BFS accumulator `bfs_dist_aux` (arbitrary fuel, depth and reached set), instantiating it at `fuel = Fintype.card α`, `depth = 1`, `reached = bfsStep {u}`, and proving it by induction on fuel.

parent.name: dist_eq_computable
parent.statement:
theorem dist_eq_computable (G : SimpleGraph α) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (u v : α) :
    G.dist u v = computable_dist G u v

children.name: mem_iterate_bfsStep_dist_le
children.statement:
lemma mem_iterate_bfsStep_dist_le (G : SimpleGraph α) [DecidableRel G.Adj]
    (u w : α) (n : ℕ) (hw : w ∈ G.bfsStep^[n] {u}) : G.dist u w ≤ n
children.closed_by: induction n generalizing w; zero case by simp; successor case by rcases on mem_bfsStep, then by_cases on a = u and on G.dist u a = 0, each branch closed with Nat.le_succ_of_le, le_trans (dist_le …) and omega
children.note: Direction (⇐) of the BFS/distance correspondence: being reached within n BFS steps bounds the distance by n.

children.name: dist_le_mem_iterate_bfsStep
children.closed_by: induction n generalizing w; zero case by rcases on hreach and Nat.le_zero; successor case by by_cases on G.dist u w ≤ n (left: ih), else right with witness p.getVert n and ih on the prefix walk p.take n
children.note: Direction (⇒) of the BFS/distance correspondence: distance at most n puts w in the n-th BFS iterate (assuming w is u or reachable).

applicability.goal_shape: An equality `G.dist u v = computable_dist G u v` between a non-computable shortest-walk distance and an executable recursive loop (`computable_dist` / `bfs_dist_aux` with a fuel counter, a depth counter and an accumulated `reached` finset), where the abstract side is defined by `SimpleGraph.dist` and the concrete side by structural recursion on fuel.
applicability.use_when: the two sides have different presentations (abstract distance vs. recursive BFS) and a direct induction would need its hypothesis generalised over the accumulator (`reached`, `depth`, fuel); state the strengthened invariant first with `suffices`, instantiate it at the concrete starting values, and run the induction inside the suffices block.
applicability.avoid_when: the strengthened invariant cannot be stated cleanly, the induction needs no generalisation so strengthening buys nothing, or the strengthened statement is not actually implied by (stronger than) the goal — a `suffices` that does not specialise back to the original goal is a false child.

claims.claim: The `shape` is a measurement: `glue_lines` = 57 (the parent proof, lines 302-358) and `child_lines` = [24, 26] (lines 250-273 and 275-300), so the 57-line glue delegates both directions of the distance bound to 50 lines of child proof.
claims.evidence: line counts at the pinned commit in https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/blob/a425ca3eb797fe927cb88c950565fdcbbbbada70/FormalConjecturesForMathlib/Combinatorics/SimpleGraph/VertexDistance.lean: 358-302+1 = 57; 273-250+1 = 24; 300-275+1 = 26; child total 50

consequences: Creates one obligation (the strengthened invariant `hsuff`) from the original equality, plus two side conditions when instantiating it at depth 1: that `bfsStep {u}` is the depth-1 iterate (closed by `simp`) and that `v` is not seen at depth 0 (closed because `v ≠ u`, from the `split_ifs` branch). The strengthened statement is quantified over arbitrary fuel/depth/reached, so its proof is an induction on fuel that must carry the invariant `h_inv` and the `h_not_found` side condition through each step. Failure mode: the invariant must be exactly right — if `h_inv` did not tie `reached` to `bfsStep^[depth] {u}`, the recurse branch could not rewrite `bfsStep reached` to `bfsStep^[depth + 1] {u}` to re-establish the induction hypothesis; and the two children must be stated as the exact two directions of `w ∈ bfsStep^[n] {u}` iff `dist u w ≤ n`, or the zero case and the `v ∈ reached` case cannot close.
